jobs.occupation: PhD student in agricultural bioeconomy systems
jobs.description:
Department of Biosystems and Technology
PhD project: Sustainable utilisation of agricultural green biomass in integrated protein and biogas systems
Subject area: Technology
Description of the doctoral project
 
A circular and fossil-independent bioeconomy requires renewable biomass without increasing competition for agricultural land and food production. Crop residues and intermediate crops are therefore particularly relevant resources. Research at SLU shows that these biomass resources can be substantial, but their potential and sustainable utilisation vary regionally. They can be used for biogas, while effects on soil carbon and nutrient cycling need to be considered.  
Green biomass can also be biorefined into plant protein for feed or food, after which the remaining streams are used for biogas. The same feedstock can thereby provide protein, energy and recycled nutrients.
The project aims to assess the potential and consequences of large-scale utilisation of green crop residues and intermediate crops in integrated biogas and green biorefinery systems.
The project will:
assess sustainably available biomass from green crop residues and intermediate crops in Sweden;
assess the potential for biogas and combined plant protein and biogas production;
develop implementation scenarios based on feedstock availability, infrastructure, logistics and markets;
assess effects on nutrient cycling, soil carbon, biomethane, fertilizer use, and feed and food production; and
evaluate economic and wider socio-economic benefits, drawbacks and trade-offs.

The project combines GIS and agricultural data with mass and nutrient balances, scenario modelling, and life cycle-based, techno-economic and socio-economic methods. Data will be drawn from research, statistics, literature and national databases.
The doctoral student will join an interdisciplinary research environment at SLU Alnarp focusing on sustainable agricultural production, bioenergy, circular bioeconomy and systems analysis.
About the position
The work includes collection and processing of agricultural and process data, GIS, modelling of biomass and product flows, scenario development, and environmental and economic assessments.  
You will integrate information from crop production and biomass availability to biorefineries, biogas, and food and energy systems.  
You will analyse data, develop models and scenarios, and publish and present research results. The work will be conducted with researchers at SLU and external partners.  
The doctoral student will be part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC), a national transdisciplinary centre where Linköping University, SLU and around 50 private and public organisations collaborate. The centre is supported by the Swedish Energy Agency. The PhD project follows BSRC’s research plans and contributes to long-term competence development in industry and academia.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in technology. To meet the specific entry requirements, you must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.  
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
You should have a Master’s degree or equivalent in, for example, biosystems/agricultural engineering, environmental engineering, agricultural science, energy systems, industrial ecology, environmental science or a related field.
Your profile
We are looking for a motivated candidate interested in sustainable agricultural and bioeconomy systems and quantitative analysis.
Experience or documented knowledge in one or several of the following areas is desirable:
systems analysis, modelling or scenario analysis;
GIS and spatial analysis;
life cycle assessment, environmental systems analysis or material-flow analysis;
techno-economic or socio-economic assessment;
bioenergy, biogas or biorefinery systems;
agricultural production systems and agricultural biomass;
statistical analysis and handling of larger datasets;
experience of programming or quantitative modelling, for example using Python, R or MATLAB.

You should have good analytical skills, be able to integrate information from different fields, work independently and collaborate well.
Excellent written and spoken English is required. Good communication skills are important. Knowledge of Swedish is advantageous but not required.
Personal qualities, motivation and the ability to successfully complete doctoral studies will be given considerable weight. 
About us
The Department of Biosystems and Technology develops knowledge for sustainable and resource-efficient agriculture, horticulture and bioeconomy through research combining biological production systems, technology and systems analysis. 
The project lies at the intersection of agriculture, biosystems engineering, sustainability assessment and bioeconomy. 
Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/
Form of employment / Funding
Employment as a doctoral student (4-year programme) 
Doctoral student’s salaries are set following the local collective agreement. Salary progression is fixed.
Location:
Alnarp, Sweden
Scope:
100%
Start date:
Upon agreement. A start date in January or February 2027 is preferred.
 
Application and selection:
 
Please submit your application using the link below. The deadline is November 27, 2026. Applications cannot be submitted through the recruitment system on 20–22 November due to a system update.
Read more about the attachments that your application should include at https://www.slu.se/en/study/programmes-courses/doctoral-education/how-can-i-become-a-doctoral-student/application/
Selection among eligible applicants is based on the documents attached to the application, and is carried out with regard to the applicant’s ability to complete the programme within the allotted time.

 Job Overview
Role Summary
Our client is seeking a Data Engineer with a focus on data catalog capabilities. This consulting assignment is central to the development and governance of metadata, data lineage, data quality, and automation within a modern data and cloud platform.
The role involves onboarding metadata from multiple source systems into the data catalog, maintaining traceability from source to consumption, and supporting data quality initiatives. Key Responsibilities
Onboard metadata from databases, reporting tools, data pipelines, APIs, and other source systems into the data catalog.
Ensure that tables, columns, reports, APIs, and related technical assets are described accurately and consistently.
Create, maintain, and improve end-to-end data lineage from source systems through transformation pipelines to downstream consumption.
Support the implementation of data quality rules and expose data quality results through the catalog.
Develop scripts and supporting tools to automate metadata ingestion and catalog-related workflows.
Integrate automation into established CI/CD pipelines.
Collaborate with Data Stewards to map technical data objects to business terms and definitions.
Work cross-functionally with engineering, DevOps, architecture, governance, and business teams.

Technical Stack & Requirements
SQL: Advanced proficiency is required.
Scripting: Experience with Python or another scripting language is preferred.
Data engineering: Practical experience with ETL/ELT processes and data pipelines.
DevOps: Experience using Git and integrating solutions into CI/CD workflows.
Data catalogs: Experience with Alation, Collibra, Microsoft Purview, or AB Initio is advantageous.
Data governance capabilities: Experience with metadata management, data lineage, and data quality frameworks is advantageous.
Platforms: Experience working with modern data and cloud platforms is beneficial.

Qualifications & Experience
You should have several years of experience as a Data Engineer, BI Developer, or in a comparable data-focused role. The assignment requires a strong interest in metadata, structured information, and data traceability. Experience from a regulated organization—particularly banking, financial services, or insurance—is advantageous. Professional fluency in both Swedish and English is required.

Design and develop mechanical components and installation solutions for battery-electric heavy-duty vehicle chassis.
Create and maintain 3D models and 2D drawings in CATIA V5 in accordance with applicable engineering and design standards.
Manage component packaging, mechanical interfaces, tolerances, and installation requirements within the chassis environment.
Develop solutions that account for manufacturability, particularly for sheet metal, plastic, and pneumatic components.
Collaborate with suppliers and cross-functional engineering teams throughout the development process.
Participate in design reviews, validation activities, and technical investigations.
Maintain accurate technical documentation and provide engineering support to production when required.

Engineering analysis: Experience performing tolerance analysis and managing dimensional requirements.
Integration: Good understanding of component packaging, mechanical interfaces, installation constraints, and chassis integration.
Manufacturing: Knowledge of design-for-manufacturing principles for sheet metal, plastic, and/or pneumatic components.
Vehicle development: Previous research and development experience involving heavy-duty vehicles.

Qualifications & Experience
A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant engineering discipline is required, together with at least three years of professional design engineering experience. Candidates must have previous R&D experience from heavy-duty vehicle development and be fluent in English. Previous experience with chassis design and component installation for heavy-duty vehicles is advantageous, as is experience spanning several of the relevant technical areas. The assignment requires the ability to drive design work independently and collaborate effectively with suppliers and cross-functional teams.
